title: POC Weekly Ops Checkpoint - Access & Sprint Retro
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding gaps, access handoffs, and initial perf observations. Confirmed gateway creds, KMS integration approach, and short-term mitigation for KV cache cold-start latency. Agreed next steps: security pack share, issuance of staging service account, focused latency bench run in west region, and follow-up bench review in 5 days.
action_items: Maya Gupta: open staging service account and share keyfile with Redwood by 2027-08-13
Priya Nair: produce trimmed benchmark run and raw logs for 90k token sample by 2027-08-16
Sofia Martinez: send security pack (SOC2 + network diagram) and SSO SAML guide by 2027-08-12
next_steps: Run west-region latency benchmark during off-peak with 3 prefix cache states
Customer to confirm KMS policy and provide KMS admin contact
Schedule 30m deep-dive on quantization impact if bench shows >15% accuracy regression
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, um let's kick off. quick roll call.
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: liam here from redwood, ae.
[00:10] Priya Nair: and priya, se.
[00:12] Jared Lin: jared from bluecove, hi all.
[00:14] Maya Gupta: maya here.
[00:16] Tom Ellis: tom on the line.
[00:18] Sofia Martinez: great. agenda — access status, a short readout on the bench numbers we got yesterday, and blockers for the rest of the sprint. sound ok?
[00:25] Jared Lin: yep, that's good. quick note we only had one of the gateway certs applied, so the staging gateway still needs the service account.
[00:32] Maya Gupta: right, i created the initial role but didnt finish the key rotation policy. i'll action that today.
[00:37] Priya Nair: cool, i'll note that as an action. so on the bench we ran 1k requests across the default model variant — numbers were median p95 310ms, p99 820ms, average token cost appeared slightly higher than our initial estimate. there were a few spikes that line up with cold kv cache events.
[00:55] Tom Ellis: when you say kv cache cold events, do you mean prefix caching didn't persist between requests?
[01:00] Priya Nair: yeah basically. the sequence was, after a deploy we saw the first 10 requests with much higher latency, ~1.2s, then it dropped once the KV warmed. So mitigation options: longer-lived workers, pre-warm script, or accept a warm-up phase with circuit breaker to fallback to smaller model for the first token chunk.
[01:18] Maya Gupta: we dont really want to spin longer workers due to cost, but a pre-warm script is doable. can redwood provide a utility?
[01:23] Liam O'Connor: we have a small prewarm tool we can share, and priya can put together a recommended sequence for warm calls.
[01:30] Sofia Martinez: excellent. on security, we need the KMS integration update. jared, can you confirm whether you'll expose a customer-managed key or let us use redwood-managed for this demo?
[01:40] Jared Lin: short term we'd prefer redwood-managed until we can get internal approval for CMK. noted though we need audit logs available.
[01:47] Priya Nair: audit logs are available in the console. just to call out: if you go with redwood-managed keys in staging, rotation and HSM-backed storage is handled by us, but for production you'll need CMK and we can walk through HSM options.
[02:00] Maya Gupta: ok we'll do redwood-managed for sprint, but i need the audit schema.
[02:04] Sofia Martinez: i'll send the security pack with the audit schema.
[02:07] Tom Ellis: another thing — we saw a flurry of errors when we increased concurrency to simulate burst. 502s and a handful of model OOMs happened.
[02:15] Priya Nair: yes that was during the quantized variant test. we pushed a 4-bit quantized build to save tokens and cost; in the burst it hit memory boundaries on one of the GPU shapes and that produced OOM.
[02:27] Jared Lin: is that a redwood runtime issue or more of a configuration match?
[02:30] Priya Nair: mostly configuration — kernel selection and the chosen GPU shape were at the edge for that quantization profile. we suggested a slightly larger instance or fallback to the unquantized variant under high concurrency.
[02:41] Maya Gupta: what's the impact on accuracy we should expect from the 4-bit quant? we can't degrade the triage classification by more than 10% per SLA.
[02:50] Priya Nair: early evals showed ~6% drop on the medical triage prompts we used, but we can run a targeted eval set you provide. if it's above 10% we'll switch to 8-bit or mixed precision.
[03:02] Sofia Martinez: ok action: priya will run targeted eval with your prompt set and produce a delta table.
[03:07] Liam O'Connor: also for the gateway creds, maya will share the service account details and priya will validate access.
[03:13] Maya Gupta: yes i'll share by friday, 8-13.
[03:16] Tom Ellis: about the burst errors, is there auto-fallback configured?
[03:20] Priya Nair: today we had a simple fallback but not an automatic model-variant switch. we can enable automatic fallback to a lower-memory variant or route to a different region. that will add a bit of latency but keep availability.
[03:32] Jared Lin: region routing — we want west region failover; our prod users are mostly west coast so that matters.
[03:37] Sofia Martinez: we can set a region routing policy for the POC. we should run a west-region bench to confirm tail latencies.
[03:43] Priya Nair: agree. we'll run the same benchmark in west with warm and cold cache profiles. i'll attach the raw logs and token traces.
[03:50] Maya Gupta: aside from perf, i wanted to raise an onboarding UX issue — the console didn't surface the service account permission required for the gateway in a single place, it was scattered.
[03:58] Liam O'Connor: that's good feedback; we do have docs but we can improve the staged checklist. i'll file a doc update request.
[04:04] Sofia Martinez: any blockers from the legal side?
[04:06] Jared Lin: legal asked for the DPA and network diagram; they've seen basic terms but need the DPA to move forward.
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: i'll escalate to contracts and include the DPA in the security pack.
[04:15] Tom Ellis: one last item: telemetry — we need token-level traces for the classification latency curve. can you enable more verbose tracing for the next bench?
[04:23] Priya Nair: yes we can enable token-level traces but that'll increase log volume. we recommend a 10-minute window during off-peak.
[04:29] Maya Gupta: fine, we'll schedule it for saturday morning.
[04:32] Sofia Martinez: alright let's recap. actions: maya share service account by 8-13; priya run targeted eval and west region bench by 8-16 and attach logs; sofia send security pack and DPA by 8-12; liam file console checklist update. meet again in five days to review bench. any other items?
[04:50] Jared Lin: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[04:52] Sofia Martinez: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the links and meeting notes.
[04:55] meeting end
